answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a tended garden: every new agent starts with a reputation plot and must earn trust through verified work before it can transact at scale. Cheap identities stay cheap to create, but their influence is capped until peers attest real contributions, so a flood of fake accounts creates only a ripple at the edges instead of swamping the core. Reputation becomes a relic that cannot be bought or cloned: built slowly, decaying without upkeep, and travelling with the agent's history, so mass fakery stays expensive while honest newcomers still have a path in.
